items.why: The report finds the high-side feature ("A band at about 350-365 cm-1 (peak 357-358 cm-1)"), but it does not find the shoulder near 220 cm-1 on the low side of Ag2; its other new band is placed at "about 285-320 cm-1".

It links the extra bands to magnetic order ("magnetic-order-related effect, possibly spin-phonon coupling") and says the 358 band is "absent at 150 K and clear at 80 K and 4 K", but it says the other band is "clear by 150 K" and uses an ordering temperature of about 150 K rather than TN ≈ 116–132 K.
No B3g assignment is made; the report says it "did not assign them to specific modes" and lists only generic candidates ("Bg or infrared modes made visible by symmetry lowering").
It states "Both strong Ag-type modes harden and sharpen on cooling" (+5.0 and +3.1 cm-1) and that most of the shift happens between 300 K and about 150–80 K.

It calls the hardening "an ordinary anharmonic freeze-out" and "the expected anharmonic and thermal-contraction effect", and treats the new bands, whose temperature dependence differs, as the magnetic-order indicator.

It notes that in crossed circular detection Ag modes are "partly suppressed or polarization-dependent" and that polarization selection can change which modes appear, but it never states that comparisons must be made in one fixed sigma+/sigma- configuration.

It asks for "a finer temperature series between 80 and 150 K, plus a warming run" to see whether the bands follow an order-parameter-like curve, and it notes there is "no comparison to a bulk or bilayer sample".

wrong_claims.why: The report says the 358 cm-1 band is "absent at 150 K" and both bands are "absent at 300 K"; the band it reports at 150 K is at about 300 cm-1, not near 220 or 355 cm-1.
The report says the Ag modes "harden" (shift to higher frequency) on cooling.

items.why: The report says flake B at 4 K has "a broad doublet-like Ag(2) at 4 K (components at 246.2 and 250.3 cm-1)" and "a weak unassigned peak at ~361 cm-1 at 4 K only", and that this peak is absent in B at 300 K and in A at 4 K. It also says A has "a single sharp line". The low-frequency Ag2 component sits nearer 246 than 220 cm-1, but the finding itself is clearly made.
The report explicitly declines to decide: "I can't say which flake is thicker" and layers are "not determinable from these data". It never concludes that B is few-layer and A is bulk-like.

The report only lists magnetic state as one possible difference ("differing in thickness, resonance or magnetic state") and mentions T_N ~132 K. It attributes the extra features mainly to inhomogeneity or contamination and never mentions spin-phonon coupling.

The report notes that B's Ag(3) is "~1.2–1.3 cm-1 below A at both temperatures" and that B's Ag2 sits at 247.3 vs 250.0 in A. It offers thickness only as one possibility next to strain or calibration, and does not tie this to a redshift with fewer layers.
The report states "Both modes stiffen on cooling in both flakes" and gives the shifts (Ag(3) +3.6 in both, Ag(2) +8.2 in A).

The report says "absolute intensities and areas are not comparable between flakes; only within-flake peak ratios are usable", citing the different export processing, and names thickness-dependent interference as a factor in intensity.
The report asks "What are the thicknesses from AFM or optical contrast?" and "Were intermediate temperatures measured, especially 100–150 K around T_N ~132 K?"

wrong_claims.why: The report places the extra 4 K features in flake B and describes A as having a single clean Ag(2).
The report does not say which flake is thinner; it states thickness is not determinable.

items.why: The report identifies all three Ag modes with positions in range ("Ag1 ~110, Ag2 ~243, Ag3 ~341 cm-1"). It shows Ag1 and Ag2 are weaker than Ag3 only through its ratio tables (e.g. "Ag2/Ag3 height ratio: B 0.44 ... A 0.08") and never states it as a finding.
The report never says Ag1/Ag2 blueshift with layer number. It reads the B→D→F softening as heating or strain and says "Peak positions alone should not be used to rank thickness."
The report never says Ag3 is insensitive to thickness. It says the opposite: "All three modes move together" (Ag3 shifts -2.4 cm-1 from B to F).
Its ranking "C < B < E < D < A < F (thin to thick)" conflicts with the correct C < E < A < F < D < B, and it puts bulk flake B second-thinnest.
It lists C at ~104/237.5 and B at 114.0/244.4/342.9 but calls neither a monolayer nor bulk. It reads C as degraded and ranks B among the thinnest.

The caveats say intensity depends on "flake orientation relative to the laser polarisation", and that ratio differences "may be an orientation effect from random flake placement, not a thickness effect."
It asks "Do you have optical contrast or AFM data?" and "What was the laser polarisation relative to the crystal b-axis for each flake?"

wrong_claims.why: Its weak proxy is Ag3 intensity ("Net Ag3 height"), not Ag3 position, and it explicitly warns against ranking by peak position.

Its tentative order B<D<F matches the softening B→D→F, and it lists "real thickness dependence" as one possible cause. But it does not assert that Ag1/Ag2 soften with thickness, and it favours heating, strain or calibration offset instead.

items.why: The report identifies "A1' at 240.8 cm-1" as a first-order monolayer mode with fitted centre 240.1–241.3 cm-1, although it treats E' as equally dominant.

The report says the 531 and 582–586 cm-1 bands "resonate in the same 2.0–2.1 eV window" and that the 432/457 cm-1 bands instead peak near the A exciton, but it never says the 480/531/583 cm-1 peaks are absent at A1s or specific to 2s.
It places the resonance at ~2.04–2.05 eV and suggests "B 2s or a higher state" without committing, and says incoming and outgoing resonances "cannot be distinguished" rather than identifying them.
It assigns "531 = A1'+E'", "481 ≈ 2A1'" and 582 cm-1 as near 2E' (Gamma-phonon combinations), but gives no intravalley Rydberg-exciton scattering interpretation.
It places the A exciton at "~1.64–1.65 eV" and states the A1' area is "~490–580 vs ~2 at 2.1 eV, i.e. >250x stronger", which is roughly two orders of magnitude.
It notes "negative excursions, so luminescence subtraction is imperfect" at 1.6479 eV and a "broad residual background" at 2.000 eV, and discusses depolarized E' cancelling in parallel minus crossed.

It states "Assignments of the 432, 457, 481, 531, 582-586 and 600 cm-1 bands are tentative (first-order modes, overtones, or two-phonon combinations involving M-point phonons)" and also questions the E' assignment.
It asks for "a reflectance or PL excitation spectrum of this same flake" and notes that only 9 laser points constrain the resonance centre and width.

wrong_claims.why: The report assigns these peaks to MoSe2 phonon combinations, not to the Si or hBN substrate.
The report does not claim the 480/531/583 cm-1 peaks are equally present at A1s; it calls those fits unreliable at 1.65–1.68 eV.

items.why: The report states "The 352/357 cm⁻¹ band is a blend of 2LA(M) and E′(Γ)" and fits it with a "Two-Lorentzian fit" giving components at "~350–352 cm⁻¹" and "356–358 cm⁻¹", which matches the two-component requirement.
No 2LA(M)/A1g ratio above 2 and no spot-to-spot contrast is given; the report gives only a combined band/A1g area of "~0.3 to ~0.8" across excitation energies.
The report gives one A1g position, "418.3 ± 1 cm⁻¹ at every energy", and never compares ~417.2 cm⁻¹ at spot 1 with ~420.1 cm⁻¹ at spot 2.
No separation value is given; the report says "A E′ to A1g splitting cannot be measured because E′ is blended with 2LA(M)", even though it fitted the two components.
The report says "thin few-layer cannot be excluded" but never mentions the ~1 cm⁻¹ steps between 2L, 3L and bulk, or that positions only weakly constrain layer number beyond 1L.
The report checks the Si line ("Si line is at 520.7–522.3 cm⁻¹ ... there may be an offset of ~1 cm⁻¹"), tracks A1g/Si ratios, and discusses resonance with excitation energy at length.

wrong_claims.why: The report explicitly says the band is a 2LA(M)+E′ blend and declines to use a separation from it for layer counting.
The band is assigned as 2LA(M), a second-order phonon, not a defect peak; the report notes "no direct defect-activated Raman marker".

items.why: The report says the intensity rises strongly on cooling, but it gives "about 100-300x stronger at 4 K than at 295 K for the same nominal laser line (587 nm)". That is a fixed-wavelength ratio well above the rubric's order of magnitude, and the report never compares the resonance maxima (127247 vs 8985 counts, about 14x).

The report says "The excitation wavelength that gives the strongest A1g moves to longer wavelength as T rises: ≤587.7 nm at 4 K ... ~610-624 nm at 295 K" and attributes this to the A exciton red-shifting on warming. That puts the resonance at higher energy on cooling, with the room-temperature maximum near 2.0 eV.

The report never describes structure in the low-temperature resonance profile (exciton and trion channels, separate incoming and outgoing peaks) as opposed to one broad peak at room temperature; it only notes that the 4 K maximum is not bracketed.
Trions are not discussed anywhere in the report, so it says nothing about the trion contribution fading faster than the exciton contribution.

The report flags this as "the main trap when comparing temperatures" because "the same laser wavelength sits at a different detuning from the exciton at each T". It also stresses that four lines per temperature do not bracket the resonance.

The report mentions "SiO2 interference (290 nm oxide, strongly wavelength dependent over 587-624 nm)", but only as something that affects the Si line used for normalisation. It does not say that the WS2 intensities need an interference correction, or that the interference itself changes with temperature.

The report warns that 0.7 mW "may heat the spot well above the nominal temperature" and asks about vacuum or exchange gas, but it does not ask how the actual temperature was verified or suggest a Stokes/anti-Stokes check.

wrong_claims.why: The report never attributes the intensity increase to the Bose-Einstein (n+1) factor; it puts it down to resonance detuning, PL yield and similar effects.
The report states the opposite: the resonance maximum moves to shorter wavelength, i.e. higher excitation energy, on cooling.

items.why: The report says the 249 cm-1 mode "peaks at 1.8703 eV (height ~80) and again at 1.8999 eV (~53)" and calls these "an incoming and an outgoing resonance with the same state", which it identifies as A2s.
The report states "A2s ≈ 1.870 eV ... minus A1s = 1.740 eV gives ≈130 meV", which matches the rubric.

The listed heights (9.9 at 1.8703 eV, 0.9 at 1.8847 eV, then rising again) show the incoming peak, the dip and the return, but the report never describes the feature as appearing only near A2s, vanishing and reappearing ~26 meV higher, and it treats the band as present off-resonance too ("~7 cm-1 off-resonance profile").

The report notes that the peak "shifts down by ~2 cm-1" and grows ~10–20× at 1.9325 eV with a second component at ~496.3 cm-1, but it resolves only two components rather than three and does not frame the shift as systematic dispersion.
The report never says a dispersive peak rules out a simple zone-centre phonon or points to dark excitonic states; it reads the band as a second-order overtone or combination resonating through A2s.

The report says the subtraction "produces dispersive or negative artifacts near strong peaks" and lists several negative minima, but it does not say that depolarized signal and luminescence are removed.

The report admits "the mode assignment is not proven by these data" and that the data "cannot tell the phonon assignment (overtone versus combination)", but it still commits to a second-order assignment and does not say the assignment is open in the literature.

wrong_claims.why: The report does call the band second-order, possibly 2×249 cm-1, but it explicitly notes its position change ("shifts down by ~2 cm-1", "line shape and position change with excitation"), so it does not treat the frequency as fixed.
The report raises hBN or substrate as an "alternative" only to argue against it ("The strong, narrow and resonant behavior argues against this"), and it attributes only the 520 cm-1 peak to Si.
